description:
Redwood Inference is expanding into more regulated enterprise workloads (Dedicated + Private deployments) where customers require least-privilege access control, provable authorization enforcement, and clear auditability. The “RBAC v2 design + permission inventory” project will (1) inventory and classify sensitive actions across the Redwood product surface area, and (2) implement a fine-grained, consistent authorization model with enforceable permission checks across API Gateway, Control Plane services, and Console/admin tooling.

Goals:
- Build a canonical permission catalog for all security-relevant actions (e.g., manage API keys, rotate secrets, modify routing policies, change model pinning/rollout, export audit logs, manage org/users/roles, configure data retention/residency, modify private deployment settings).
- Define RBAC v2 primitives (permissions, roles, role bindings, scopes such as org/project/environment/cluster) and map them to product workflows.
- Implement deny-by-default enforcement with consistent middleware/interceptors, plus safe exemptions (break-glass) and migration support.
- Ensure auditability: log authorization decisions (who/what/why) and produce evidence-friendly artifacts for SOC2/enterprise questionnaires.
- Provide operator UX: role templates, permission viewer, and “why was I denied?” guidance.

Scope:
- In-scope: Hosted API + Console + Control Plane endpoints; Dedicated and Private admin operations; policy bundle repo for roles/permissions; audit log schema updates for authz decision fields.
- Out-of-scope (for v2): full ABAC/policy language exposed to customers, custom per-customer rule scripting, and a full re-architecture of identity (SSO integration remains, but RBAC is the authorization layer).

Key stakeholders and teams:
- Security & Compliance: Dr. Aisha Rahman (exec sponsor), Marcus Lin (Security Eng), Kevin Osei (audit logging/export), Olga Petrov (GRC), Daniel Carter (evidence).
- Engineering: Priya Natarajan (Platform leadership), Ethan Park (Platform Control Plane), Jordan Lee (policy engine), Kaitlyn Nguyen (authn/authz integration), Amara Diallo (API Gateway).
- Product: Naomi Feldman (Security & Compliance PM), Vivek Kulkarni (Private Deployments PM).
- Operational partners: David Kim (IT/identity + internal admin), Fiona McCarthy (SecOps), Colin O'Donnell (Solutions Eng for Private customer pilots).

Timeline (phased, with overlapping tracks):
1) Discovery & inventory (2–4 weeks): enumerate actions, data objects, existing checks, and gaps; define naming conventions and sensitivity tiers.
2) Design (3–5 weeks): RBAC v2 model, scope semantics, migration and compatibility strategy, audit log schema, and performance approach (caching, evaluation locality).
3) Implementation (6–10 weeks): shared authorization library + service adoption; policy bundle generation; Console/admin UX; tests and rollout tooling.
4) Rollout & validation (4–8 weeks): internal dogfood, feature-flagged customer pilots (especially Private), documentation, support playbooks, and compliance evidence packaging.

Key deliverables:
- Permission inventory + role/permission matrix.
- RBAC v2 design + ADRs.
- Implemented permission checks across critical services with CI coverage.
- Updated audit logging to include authorization decision context.
- Customer- and internal-facing documentation (security FAQ, runbooks, migration guides).

Constraints:
- Backwards compatibility during migration (avoid breaking existing API keys/roles).
- Performance: authorization checks must be low-latency and deterministic; caching must be safe and correctly scoped.
- Multi-deployment support: Hosted, Dedicated, and Private must share semantics while allowing environment-specific scoping.
- Secure defaults: deny-by-default, minimal implicit permissions, clear break-glass controls with monitoring.

files.description: Primary RBAC v2 design doc: goals, non-goals, entities (permissions/roles/bindings/scopes), evaluation flow, storage model, caching strategy, and rollout plan with compatibility notes.
Canonical permission catalog: action naming conventions, sensitivity tiers, resource types, and a table mapping existing endpoints/jobs to permissions (including gaps and ownership).
Proposed built-in roles (e.g., Org Admin, Security Admin, Billing Admin, Read-only Auditor, Deployment Operator) with an explicit permission matrix and rationale.
Migration plan from RBAC v1/coarse roles: dual-read/dual-write strategy, feature flags, default mappings, deprecation timeline, and risk mitigation.
Break-glass design: emergency admin procedure, approval workflow, time-bound elevation, logging/alerting requirements, and post-use review.
Audit log schema extension to include authorization decisions: subject, action, resource scope, policy version, decision (allow/deny), and denial reasons.
Customer-facing internal guidance for Support/CS/SE: how to explain RBAC v2, recommended role setups, and common troubleshooting for permission-denied issues.
Engineering standard for where/how to enforce authorization (gateway vs service), required endpoint annotations, error semantics, and test requirements.
ADR deciding permission string format, namespacing, and versioning rules (including deprecation policy and compatibility guarantees).
ADR comparing centralized authz service vs embedded library evaluation; decision, trade-offs, and operational implications.
PRD: problem statement, user personas (Security Admin, Platform Operator), functional requirements, metrics of success, and phased release plan.
Console UX spec: role editor, role templates, permission viewer/search, assignment flows, and 'why denied' UX; includes edge cases and accessibility notes.
Updated security FAQ entry set for Sales/SE: RBAC scope model, auditability, SSO interaction, and common questionnaire answers.
Operational runbook for rollout: enabling flags, monitoring error rates/denies, rollback steps, and coordination checklist across gateway/control plane.
Working notes from cross-functional workshops: list of candidate sensitive actions, open questions on scopes, and disagreements/trade-offs.
Engineering scratchpad with diagrams-in-text for request flow (gateway -> service), caching ideas, and proposed library APIs.
Sheet-style doc: draft role-to-permission matrix with columns for Hosted/Dedicated/Private applicability and notes on default mappings.
Draft responses to common enterprise security questionnaires focusing on RBAC granularity, audit logs, retention, and admin controls.

Rough UI outline/wire notes for role management screens and permission search/filter behavior; includes feedback bullets from reviewers.
Risk register: potential breakages, denial spikes, internal admin workflows impacted, mitigation steps, and owners.
Audit of current endpoints/jobs with flags for missing checks, inconsistent error semantics, and suggested permission mapping.
